text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Price of new telephone lines may soon be cut to some 700 kuna from 3,500 kuna, approaching usual prices in western Europe, deputy director of state post and telecommunications board Mladen Sutalo said.

- Croatian border with Hungary in the Baranja area, so far under supervision of the U.N. transitional authority (UNTAES), has been used as a regular escape route by smugglers of stolen cars, arms and other goods, according to Hungarian customs officers.

- Jadranka Cigelj from Prijedor who will testify in The Hague against late indicted war criminal Simo Drljaca, recently shot dead in NATO raid in Bosnia, confirms that he had helped to set up notorious prison camps of Omarska, Keraterm and Trnopolje in northern Bosnia.

- Half of some 5,000 Serb families who now live in the last Serb enclave of Eastern Slavonia soon to revert to Zagreb rule, wish to sell their property and leave the country. Half are to be resettled to their original homes across Croatia, Reconstruction Minister Jure Radic said at a government session.
- Czechs, Germans, Austrians and Slovenians are the most numerous among 300,000 guests who now rest at the Adriatic coast, but Italians will outnumber them in August.
- Marketing experts criticise new Croatian tourist slogan "Croatia - Paradise On Earth" as pretentious, clumsy and overused.

- Croatian trade unions protest against World Bank recommendation that Croatian government cut salaries in public sector claiming Bank's analysis is founded on outdated information. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
